action_needed: Map tiles now come through the server, which needs outbound HTTPS to the tile providers; an installation without a public address loads OpenStreetMap in the browser instead.
The official servers moved to master7.dedalo.dev; beta7.dedalo.dev is an opt-in beta provider
An ontology server accepts the access codes listed in ONTOLOGY_SERVERS; ONTOLOGY_SERVER_CODE is retired.
Dédalo now runs on Bun 1.4.4, the latest stable release.
Irreversible maintenance actions now require the superuser, maintenance mode and a recent backup.

entries.title: Thesaurus indexation badges: white text in the light theme, a readable brown tint in the dark theme.
JSON fields save when you leave them, like every other field.
Field names cut short in the edit form show in full on hover.
Field labels in the edit form are easier to read on Mac.
An empty list no longer looks like a warning.
Required fields that are still empty no longer look like errors.
Portal rows no longer glow on hover; only section list rows do.
Background is now the default active-field style; Frame becomes one of the choices.
Sorting a portal by a column header is now a temporary view; **Save** makes it the stored order.
On a phone, portal tables now show as labelled cards like section lists, with the drag handle always visible.
The field you are editing is now outlined by an orange frame instead of a light orange background.
A portal whose ontology declares an order now stores its records in that order.
Section lists and portals now place their rows with the row box. Long lists stay fast, scrolling never loses an edit, and screen readers announce each list as a table or a list.
JSON fields are lighter and faster
Geolocation maps load faster
The text editor toolbar stays in view while you scroll a long text.
Audiovisual records load faster and reuse cached media.
Pages open noticeably faster for returning users on slow connections.
AI entry points are hidden when the installation has no model.
Link fields show their hints only on hover or when selected.
Images, PDFs, SVGs and 3D models load faster and reuse cached files.
The search panel opens in one smooth step instead of stuttering in.
Tools that open in a dialog appear about half a second sooner on slow connections.
The Transcription and Translation tools' text panes now look like the Indexation tool's.
Tree-picker portals show their linked records like Parent and Children.
An empty date field is now blank until you hover or select it.
The inspector's Relations, Latest changes and Component history panels now page the same way.
Developer builds are named for the next version, for example 7.0.1-dev.
Terms can be reordered while a thesaurus or ontology search is showing the tree.
The active-field style list gains Background, the tinted-surface look Dédalo used before the styles existed (it is the default).
Each user can now choose how the field being edited is highlighted: Frame, Lift or Margin.
Press ⌘K (Ctrl+K) to jump to any section or open a tool.
Indexation, transcription and translation tools — time machine button on the text
"Ontology CSS: responsive rules no longer overwrite each other, area styles apply, edits show at once."
In the search panel, a portal field's search options are wide enough to use, and the results no longer cover them.
A split search in a linking field finds records that match every part.
URL fields take less room and no longer clip their buttons on phones.
The JSON editor toolbar fits narrow windows and shows when there is something to save.
Long lists (hundreds of records per page) scroll smoothly again.
The term picker opened from a field has a Close button instead of the area's tools.
Text editors, URL fields and record pickers fit better, especially on phones.
Thesaurus and ontology tree badges are easier to read, and the inline JSON editor keeps its width.
Portal search results show each record as one line of text, with its columns aligned.
Typing a search in a portal's search box no longer counts as an unsaved change.
The interface is now fully translated into every supported language.
Clicking a value in a list cell opens it for editing in a window, portals included, without activating the table around it.
The id cell's hover text is now readable on its orange, green and red fills.
Lists separate multiple values again instead of gluing them together.
PDF and SVG fields show the placeholder when their file is missing.
Portals inside a portal table use the space of their column and no longer cover neighbouring rows.
Portal tables, their search box and full-screen view are tidier and use space better.
The user activity statistics are now translated.
The filter_records search field scrolls inside its card instead of spilling over the next one.
The login screen shows your own user image while it loads.
Columns declared for a nested portal now show everywhere it appears, in every mode and on every page.
A portal row’s reorder handle is fully visible and grabbable again.
A search field no longer jumps when you click it
The record's Id badge can be selected to show its information in the inspector.
Uploading a very large file no longer reports an error while the server is still joining it.
The Projects checklist in edit mode fills its whole field instead of stopping halfway.
Wide portal tables in edit mode scroll sideways instead of sliding under the inspector.
A long text area stays inside its field — idle or active — and no longer widens itself on load.
An activated text area no longer spills its text past the field and over the component below it.
Tool panes: the editor fills its frame, the toolbar lines up with it, and Lift/Margin keep their mark inside tools.
A term duplicated in the thesaurus/ontology tree can be reordered right away.
Thesaurus/ontology tree — a term dropped onto a closed term no longer hides that term's other children, and reordering works after showing non-descriptors.
Screen readers now announce the list delete and edit buttons.
Screen readers now announce the language and dashboard selectors.
The menu no longer offers the retired Graphs area.
Area dashboards, the thesaurus and ontology toolbars, the Maintenance map and the edit inspector fit a phone screen.
A field whose save failed is no longer forgotten — it stays marked unsaved and is saved again.
Dragging a related record on the second page of a portal now moves it where it is dropped.
Components with language versions show the other version beside the value, and offer the translation tool
Records open when a portal's list layout names a field from an uninstalled ontology.
Catalog terms show the coins of their type again, and legend symbols follow their legend.
Portals without a configured page size show their paginator again.
Open relationships now follows every found record, with exact counts per related section.
Search panel no longer forced tall by the fields list
Reordering a related record to an invalid position no longer removes it.
The export now writes the data language you select in the tool, not always the main one.
Indexation — the text pane's header now matches the selected field.
Indexation shows the orange unsaved-changes bar on its text boxes.
The side panel of a record that does not exist no longer offers record actions.
The search panel's side lists now always end level with the search fields.
A list could show the previous search's record total.
The thesaurus search Type list no longer grows taller than the Fields list.
Clicking inside a tall field no longer scrolls the page.
An active text field keeps its label visible above the editor toolbar.
A Time Machine note can be written again on every change in Component history.
The cataloguing tool shows only its own thesauri, marks used types, and shows every configured coin again.
Translation tool — full screen works again, and the read-only source has no save button.
Tool save notices are readable again and no longer cover the close button.
The menu no longer offers Maintenance or Development to users whose profile does not grant them.
A saved search whose field no longer exists in the ontology no longer breaks the search panel.
Three sections with ontology defects now open, or say clearly why they cannot.
Four tools that failed to open, or did more than asked, are fixed.
Your user settings show your profile, and selection lists no longer show another user's labels.
Opening a record you cannot access shows the no-access page, and the Relations panel appears only when you may read it.
The inspector's Component history keeps all its rows after you add a note, and pages through long histories.
Uploading an image from the text editor toolbar works again.
Paging to the last records of a large section is fast for users limited to their projects.
User profile editor opens for ordinary users
A user who may write a relation field can now search and pick its target records without a read grant on the target section.
Ontology updates now check every downloaded file against the master's digest before importing it.
The relations of a record are only shown to users who can open that record.
A link to a single field of a record outside your projects is refused like a link to the record.
An ontology server accepts the access codes listed in ONTOLOGY_SERVERS; ONTOLOGY_SERVER_CODE is retired.
The Ontologies screen offers domain ontologies only, with English group names everywhere.
The running install step shows its time counting up.
The ontology update lists what a server offers by name, and several ontology servers can be used side by side.
Map tiles now come through the server, which needs outbound HTTPS to the tile providers; an installation without a public address loads OpenStreetMap in the browser instead.
The official servers moved to master7.dedalo.dev; beta7.dedalo.dev is an opt-in beta provider
An ontology master can promote chosen tlds from another provider.
The code update panel is simpler — the installed version, what blocks an update and how to fix it, everything else folded away.
A column defined with a level-two `section_tipo: "self"` is no longer shown; the new `ddo_self_depth` check lists every such definition.
The ontology now stores model, table and column names as language-free machine names.
Dédalo now runs on Bun 1.4.4, the latest stable release.
/health shows only the state of an update run and of the data version, not their identifiers.
Irreversible maintenance actions now require the superuser, maintenance mode and a recent backup.
The ontology update lists the nodes it will remove or re-model, and a failed update says exactly what it restored.
The section-id repair script now checks for a recent backup before it writes.
The TOOLS_ENABLE_REGISTRY_IMPORT setting is retired; a code update now always re-registers tools and keeps each one's Active choice.
Update ontology says whether a database backup is in place before you press the button.
An ontology update only touches the shared ontologies.
A code update is now one journaled update run that also applies the ontology, schema, data and tool steps, and confirms only after verifying them.
Update runs refuse ontology sources without file digests and resume more safely.
After an update that needs a database restore, no new update starts until the run is closed.
Updates check what the master offers, and masters must use https.
AI tools are hidden when no AI model is configured.
The Update code panel shows its options only once loaded, and maintenance mode is switched on from the update dialog only.
The publication tool asks for the number of pending deletions without using the retry action.
The code update panel tells you about maintenance mode up front and lets you switch it on there.
The Docker install guide says the Official image comes from GitHub Container Registry only, and that the Docker Hub mirror is reached through a custom image.
The Docker install's System checks show cosign, and the Image version help names only the tags the installer accepts.
The installer shows that the image pull is alive, and says when docker has gone silent.
Resuming an interrupted Docker install asks for the root password once, not twice.
The Docker install guide lists the curl, unzip, sha256sum and cosign prerequisites, and documents the updater's --check dry run.
The installer Review lists the cosign verify command for an official image, and the registry check reports success.
Production, Docker and Trial installs keep a log of the run.
The installer sets the installation's public address (`DEDALO_HOST`), which map tiles and geo services identify it with.
The Publication server API panel can open the v2 API documentation.
Profile permissions can be discarded before saving.
The permissions tree filter can show the siblings of a found item.
Older images in rich text can be made visible on published pages, from Maintenance.
The container updater gains a --check dry run that reports whether an update would be accepted, without changing anything.
Install guides: Debian without sudo, PostgreSQL 18 on older Ubuntu, Docker on RHEL, boot-time 502.
An air-gapped install makes no GeoIP download.
The terminal installer says why it refuses a choice.
The developer install's final screen lists only addresses its certificate covers.
The Docker host record reports the generated salt like the engine's record.
The firewall verdict stays visible after a passing System check.
The interactive installer asks for a local ontology package under either update-server answer.
The installer checks that a local ontology source is readable before it changes anything.
The bootstrap run as root leaves nothing in `/root/.bun`.
A default exactly as wide as a text field is shown whole.
An unpublished image is no longer reported as an unverified deletion on a copy publication host.
Style changes reach browsers right after a code update, whatever the web server's cache headers.
The maintenance System Map follows the interface language.
A reconcile apply that is refused now says why, and the Reconcile panel can narrow a run.
The Bun-runtime procedure finds an instance whose name contains dots.
The root user can now open their own account panel by clicking their name in the header.
The newest update run is always the one shown as newest.
A code update on an installation without an ontology server no longer stops in "needs a database restore".
The data update refuses a step meant for a newer version than the running code.
An interrupted Docker image update now rolls back instead of leaving the stack pinned to an unverified version.
Restoring a code copy asks for confirmation whenever the code changes, also between betas.
A code update whose database migration fails is no longer confirmed.
Older development builds are offered the nightly again
Patch releases are offered when the data version did not change.
The test ontology is no longer shipped or offered to installations.
After login, users open on the default section set in their user record.
Menu entries a user may open no longer disappear when their parent area is hidden from that user.
The root user's "My profile" tool opens again.
The host `--status --json` on the Docker and trial routes reports the install record the run wrote.
A commit with a release tag is never built as a development build, and Docker says plainly that it has no nightly images.
The reconcile panel no longer reports "OK" when it found images it cannot fix.
The permissions tree filter no longer freezes after several searches.
Setting permissions on a large area is faster, and a failed change no longer locks the permissions tree.
The container updater reports a refused re-install of the pinned release as its own outcome, same_version, instead of downgrade_refused.
The installer's --plain mode refuses answer flags before it asks any question, and names the flags it refused.
Ontology update and export now say why the ontology directory cannot be created.
The Reconcile panel's table is readable: each reconcile's name sits above its description, headers read as headers, and Check / Apply stay on one line.
Images inserted into rich text are visible on published pages.
Profile permissions search: a matched section or area now shows its permission radios and can be opened.
The updater's same-version refusal suggests the skip flag only for a stack pinned at a bare version.
Installing or updating no longer leaves a hidden `.<hash>-<pid>.node-gyp` folder in the Dédalo folder.
The official Docker image now carries its signature in every registry that publishes it
Interface labels are a separate, cacheable download — `get_environment` and `start` no longer carry `get_label`.
Tool-owned panels outside the tool window can wear the tool's colour
Nested reads carry a verified caller chain; the client's `show` and search query are checked; a level-two `self` in a client map is refused with a notice.
Database migrations are frozen by content hash.
A release tag needs its catalog entry and its seed.
Four read-path comparison tests now expect the current ontology definitions.
Tools can look up places, parcels and elevations through one checked door.
A geolocation value can now carry its map sources and a legend.
A tool action that only reads can declare itself read-only, so a failed lookup shows its real error.
Tools can now explain a refusal in the user's own language.
Section lists, portals and the tool mosaics place their rows through one client module, the record window, with a fixed row DOM contract.
The parity test baseline can be re-recorded in the CI image.
The test suites refuse to run at the same time on one test database.
`bun run test:crawl` checks every feature as an administrator and as a project-scoped editor.
A write sent with an unusable retry count is no longer resent without its duplicate-protection key.
The test ontology's "Countermark descriptions" section tool now opens its target section.
The section read example in the API field mapping names the section in source.tipo and lists it in sqo.section_tipo.
